data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace is a Series G-stage space and aerospace company founded by Bryan Dean that has raised $20M to date. The valuation landscape includes 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning the sector, though narrow same-stage and similar-tier peer sets are limited.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable method, anchors valuation to the $41M total-raised proxy and applies a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical for Series G advancement, yielding $51M. This approach is supported by observed company progression patterns but reflects capital deployment rather than fundamental performance metrics. Peer-median analysis is not viable; while 14 same-sector private companies exist, insufficient depth at the same stage or adjacent tier (fewer than 3 datapoints meeting filter criteria) precludes reliable median derivation. Public-comp anchoring via the Space & Aerospace sector P/S median of 27.4x cannot be applied due to absent revenue disclosure—standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $44M to $59M, centered at $51M. This range rests primarily on a single triangulation method, creating meaningful uncertainty around the point estimate. Key unknowns include Dragonfly's revenue trajectory, customer concentration, and technical de-risking progress relative to peers. Without disclosed financials or tighter comparable benchmarking, investors should treat this valuation as indicative rather than definitive.
